text:
Yes — this reads as a real, operating business, and nothing in the selected insights is a reason to stop.

The substantive positives: the submitted name matches a New York registration, that registration is active in the formation state, and watchlist screening came back with no hits. For an SMB account that is the core of what you need — a legally existing entity, currently in good order, not on a list.

Two things look like gaps but are not findings against the business. New York does not publish a good-standing sub-status at all, so that question has no answer available anywhere — it tells you nothing about this applicant. And the officer check found no match for Joshua Gee because the only officer New York publishes on this filing is the PLLC itself, listed for service of process. That is how the state files professional LLCs; it is not evidence that Joshua Gee is unconnected to the business, only that the registry has nothing to compare him against.

The one thing worth noting rather than acting on: you have no independent confirmation of who controls this entity. The officer check could not supply it, and nothing else you selected speaks to it. If your policy needs a named control person verified, that is the gap to close — through a document or a person-level check — not something these insights can answer either way.
